nodes.description: Because the mechanism converges on TNF-driven inflammation and cell death, TNF inhibition is directly disease-modifying. In P1, etanercept improved the arthritis but colitis persisted; after a switch to adalimumab the colitis markedly diminished and inflammatory biomarkers normalized, giving complete clinical and transcriptomic resolution. In P2, etanercept reduced fever episodes.

nodes.description: LUBAC normally restrains assembly of the death-inducing complex downstream of the TNF receptor and promotes NF-kappaB pro-survival signalling. With LUBAC impaired, cells become hypersensitive to TNF-induced death, predominantly apoptosis, with only a limited necroptotic contribution in the human disease. The resulting cell death drives tissue inflammation.

nodes.description: The chronic proliferative dermatitis (cpdm) mouse carries a spontaneous Sharpin loss-of-function mutation and develops TNF-dependent multi-organ inflammation and immunodeficiency through excess RIPK1-dependent cell death. It is the long-studied model of SHARPIN loss, but it diverges from the human disease in a clinically important way.
